newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Employment Dept jobs indicator rises.
newsitem.headline: Australian Employment Dept jobs indicator rises.

text.p: The Australian government's leading indicator of employment rose to minus 0.494 in February from minus 0.531 in January, the Employment Department said on Wednesday.
Earlier figures had been revised by the Department of Employment, Education Training and Youth Affairs (DEETYA), as usual.

"The revision of the DEETYA leading indicator points to a trough in the indicator in November 1996, suggesting an increase in the rate of employment growth later in 1997," the department said in a statement.
"It will still be a few months, however, before we can determine whether there has in fact been a trough, or just a fluctuation similar to that which occurred over late 1995 and early 1996."
The indicator is an amalgam of seven statistical series, including vehicle registrations, housing approvals and job vacancies.
Since the early 1980s, it has consistently anticipated turns in the labour market -- beginning to rise or fall before employment does -- but with highly variable lags.
